source.text:
10. And when a straight-line stood upon (another)
straight-line makes adjacent angles (which are) equal to
one another, each of the equal angles is a right-angle, and
the former straight-line is called a perpendicular to that
upon which it stands.

source_claims.requirement: Represent the standing/base-line configuration with the correct incidence and participant roles.
Bind adjacency to the two angles generated by that configuration.
Preserve the equality condition on those adjacent angles.

source_claims.source_quote: each of the equal angles is a right-angle
source_claims.requirement: Identify both equal adjacent angles as right angles, not only one arbitrary angle.

source_claims.source_quote: the former straight-line is called a perpendicular to that upon which it stands
source_claims.requirement: Bind perpendicularity to the standing and base lines in the stated order.

interpretation_decisions.question: How are adjacent-angle equality and the right-angle classification encoded?
If orthogonality or a numeric angle is substituted, what source-to-model correspondence justifies it?

review_failure_probes: A dot-product-zero predicate with no connection to the source adjacent-angle configuration is not sufficient evidence by itself.
